subject: ClearCare model-eval: dataset format, recommended models & scoring criteria
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Duncan <alex.duncan@clearcarehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: ClearCare model-eval: dataset format, recommended models & scoring criteria

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment before you send the sample dataset:

Summary of what we discussed:
- Goal: run a customer-specific evaluation to validate triage + note-synthesis accuracy for the Care Triage flow (clinical intake -> recommended next steps).
- Data scope: 10k de-identified encounters for initial run (mix of urgent/non-urgent), CSV export from your EHR team with a single row per encounter.
- Primary KPIs: intent accuracy (top-1), hallucination rate (clinically incorrect assertions), average token latency, and QA F1 on labeled entities.

Immediate asks (action items):
1) Alex / ClearCare: share a sample CSV (500 rows) with the schema we discussed by Friday so we can sanity-check format and do an initial smoke-run. Recommend including columns: encounter_id, patient_age, raw_notes, presenting_complaint, annotated_triage_label (gold), annotations_json (optional).
2) Redwood: provide an eval runbook + recommended model list and scoring rubric. Ben and Karthik are copying in the runbook + rubric link below.
3) Procurement: once scope is agreed we’ll send a short SOW and timeline (2–3 week initial eval cadence).

Recommended models (initial):
- redwood-3b-int8 (cost-efficient baseline)
- redwood-7b-q4 (quality + latency balance)
- redwood-13b (high-quality reference run; will be slower and more expensive)

Notes on regression guardrails:
- We’ll baseline against the current production model you listed on the call (v-prod-2.1). Any model whose hallucination rate increases by >3 percentage points or whose intent accuracy drops by >4% relative to baseline triggers a regression flag and block for rollout.
- We’ll instrument a canary rollout (5% traffic) and a gated A/B with automatic fallback to v-prod-2.1 if the canary fails the smoke checks.

Links/attachments we’ll send in follow-up: runbook + sample scoring scripts + SOW draft. Ben — feel free to add details on dataset format and scoring below.

Thanks — Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com

--
Attachment: redwood-eval-runbook.md (text) — includes sample scorer and expected CSV schema
From: Alex Duncan <alex.duncan@clearcarehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearcarehealth.com
Date: 2026-12-01T18:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: ClearCare model-eval: dataset format, recommended models & scoring criteria

Thanks, Ava — appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications before we send the sample export:

- PHI/PII: we will de-identify patient names and MRN but keep age (in years) and encounter timestamps. Is that acceptable for the scoring scripts?
- annotations_json: will that be a free-form JSON column with entity spans and label ids? We can provide both a simplified gold label column and a full annotation column — would you prefer both?
- Timeline: the team here is aiming for the sample by Friday; procurement is reviewing the SOW draft now.

Also — would like to confirm the scoring thresholds you mentioned. Can you send the rubric in a machine-readable format (CSV/JSON) that we can import into our QA tools?

On the model choices — we’re open to starting with the 7B quantized model if it shows comparable intent accuracy to your 13B run. Cost is a consideration.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Duncan
Head of ML Engineering | ClearCare Health
alex.duncan@clearcarehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Duncan <alex.duncan@clearcarehealth.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearCare model-eval: dataset format, recommended models & scoring criteria

Alex — quick reply with the machine-readable rubric and dataset schema attached. See the run-through below and the attachments/links in the Drive/GitHub.

Attachment summary (also in the Drive folder):
- clearcare-sample-annotations.csv (CSV sample, 250 rows)
- redwood-eval-runbook.md (markdown with commands and scorer)
- benchmark-suite.zip (contains scoring scripts and runners)
- SLA_and_SOW_draft.pdf (SOW + proposed timeline)

Dataset schema (expected columns) — please mirror exactly to avoid parsing surprises:
- encounter_id: string
- encounter_timestamp: ISO 8601 string
- patient_age: integer (years)
- raw_notes: text (free-form clinician notes)
- presenting_complaint: short text
- annotated_triage_label: categorical (urgent, routine, refer) — gold label for intent
- annotations_json: optional JSON string with entity spans (start_idx, end_idx, label)

Scoring rubric (machine-readable keys in redwood-eval-runbook.md):
- intent_top1_accuracy (percent)
- intent_top3_accuracy (percent)
- entity_f1 (micro)
- hallucination_rate (percent of outputs containing verifiably incorrect clinical assertions)
- avg_latency_ms (generation + post-processing)
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd

Regression policy (applies to all model variants):
- Block rollout if hallucination_rate increases by >= 3.0 percentage points vs baseline
- Block rollout if intent_top1_accuracy drops by >= 4.0 percentage points vs baseline
- Alert if avg_latency_ms increases by >20% vs baseline

Recommended quick-run commands (from runbook):
- python run_eval.py --model redwood-7b-q4 --input clearcare-sample-annotations.csv --out results/7b-q4.json
- python score_results.py --gold clearcare-sample-annotations.csv --pred results/7b-q4.json --metrics out/7b-q4-metrics.csv

Benchmark links:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-redwood-clearcare-eval
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-suites/clearcare-bench

Notes on privacy: our scoring runners can operate inside your VPC/private deployment if you prefer. For hosted runs we redact tokens flagged as names/IDs before storing intermediate artifacts. Let us know which option you prefer when you share the sample.

Next steps from our side:
- We’ll run the 7B quantized and 3B-int8 as quick smoke tests the day we receive the sample.
- If the sample looks clean, we’ll schedule a 45-min review session with your ML team to walk through results (recommended within 3 business days of sample receipt).

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

--
Attachments included: clearcare-sample-annotations.csv, redwood-eval-runbook.md, benchmark-suite.zip, SLA_and_SOW_draft.pdf

Cheers, Alex
